steps.label: Start with the question
steps.human:
Supply the original research question and optional restrictions. The host supplies authorized workspace and source context; the question caller does not select a query operation.

The public research route conditionally interprets needs before evidence retrieval when an authorized configured graph source applies and no explicit answer_requirements were supplied. Direct registered-operation requests and native-only research remain separate compatible paths. [Public guide](docs/how-to/kernel-query-growth.md).

The checked research contract contains the caller's question; the checked neutral request contract below describes the separate direct-operation entry. Sending both is not required.

steps.label: Interpret all information needs together
steps.human:
Read the host packet and input artifact, then propose all five selections and uncertainties in one response: entity types, target IDs, required fields, document types and relationships. Keep original_question and source_scope unchanged. This step interprets the need; it does not retrieve evidence or answer the question.

selections are required information; uncertain records unresolved choices. detail_mode controls fields versus document/context detail. completeness distinguishes an exact item, a chosen set, exhaustive enumeration and examples. hierarchy_scope controls root or parent inclusion; hierarchy_levels contains only explicit L0–L3 filters, with [] meaning all levels. scope_resolution identifies missing user meaning versus source discovery.

For obligations questions, criteria is the authoritative acceptance-clause field; test_spec only supplements it. Unsupported meaning uses the standalone needs_outside_catalog entry in unresolved, with prose kept separately. A structurally accepted proposal is not proof of semantic correctness. Model identity and usage are unknown without actual host usage receipts. [Host instructions and checks](kernel/capabilities/host/retrieval_needs.py).

steps.label: Validate and carry the interpretation forward
steps.human:
Validate the submission against the pending host request before accepting it: unchanged question and scope, offered labels, disjoint selected/uncertain values and bounded output. The existing ledger records acceptance and resumes the same research run.

A decided interpretation is projected into answer_requirements and retained as retrieval_needs on child retrieval requests. required_fields stays the answer obligation; unsupported population mappings stay unresolved. Explicit hierarchy_levels and hierarchy_scope map to scope.levels and scope.inclusion. The same projection serves catalog-configured and catalog-absent retrieval.

Missing user meaning takes the existing bounded human continuation and reinterprets only after new clarification. Unsupported meaning or failed prerequisites return an explicit partial evidence bundle. No host response grants graph-write or query-admission permission. [Projection](integrations/research_needs.py), [dispatch](kernel/capabilities/research/planning.py) and [request contract](kernel/contracts/payloads.py).

Examples show a valid illustrative handoff; they do not establish a real retrieved answer.

This bounded integration supports field projection. full_document and unsupported or multiple relationship obligations return an explicit unresolved outcome rather than a smaller fulfilled answer. Admitted entity queries can be selected with their verified digest, but creating a new query still uses the existing component-scoped build contract; an arbitrary target cannot be converted into a misleading component clarification.

Counts retain result, byte, candidate and depth bounds. The default top_k of 6 cannot establish an exhaustive 15-descendant count; such a result remains partial without an exact total. Metadata can use safe projected field values and field locators, while canonical criteria use immutable source disclosure. A missing final answerability judgment due to budget exhaustion also remains partial.

Execution accepts fields mode and one mapped entity/document pair: ac/ac_yaml, adr/adr, ticket/ticket, component/component, flow/flow or decision/decision. Multiple pairs, bounded_context, full_document or unsupported document types return unresolved before querying; returned entity kind must match. The shared standalone interpreter can describe broader needs without making them executable in this route.

steps.label: Check whether the data can answer it
steps.human:
Check supported kinds, relationships and required fields before a missing-query build can be offered.

Missing data, an unsupported mapping, an undisclosed field and an unknown capability are different from a missing query. An existing operation may still return useful partial evidence, but a coding agent is not asked to invent absent source facts. Pre-selection support does not itself prove that an operation is missing. [Capability-fit boundary](knowledge/capability_fit.py) · [Explicit graph nodes](integrations/query_graph.py).

I/O boundary: The dictionary schema is a reviewed transcription of the real producer. The graph transforms missing_query to supported_data_pending_selection before catalog selection; true build permission still needs separate checks.

steps.human:

I/O boundary: The research graph judges bounded evidence through JevResult. This illustrative transport result does not erase deterministic assessment limitations and is not a live quality receipt.

I/O boundary: kernel/capabilities/research/collect.py uses purpose research.assess. With this partial single item it may ask evaluable; satisfied-need answer checks and conflict questions are conditional. The answer is a NOUL probability, not a query choice.

steps.label: Return the answer, limits and next step
steps.human:
Return attributable evidence and an honest outcome. Preserve a waiting run for a specific human or agent response; stop when limits or unresolved facts prevent more progress.

Partial all-required research can expose its existing evidence bundle without becoming completed. Observations describe the final bounded outcome; standalone tracing is opt-in. A candidate trace URL is not proof of remote ingestion. Observation failure does not trigger a second retrieval or destroy the result. [Public result](kernel/service_envelope.py) · [App-owned observation](integrations/knowledge_observation.py) · [Diagnosis](integrations/knowledge_diagnosis.py).

I/O boundary: KernelService wraps capability output and durable pending interactions. The raw payload object uses its companion schema id; it is not automatically a retrieval-needs output.

Example boundary: The same partial bundle reaches the caller as status partial. This is a terminal partial example; waiting_host/waiting_human use their own matching interaction records.

For the typed-needs path, assessments[need_id] retains the actual answer assessment with kind=retrieval_answer, including original_question, required_fields, scope, missing fields and completeness. Existing conditional assessments keep their prior envelope. Successful evidence collection cannot replace missing final answerability proof.

acceptance_scenarios.given: Required facts, population or inputs are ambiguous

acceptance_scenarios.given: Required facts, population or inputs are ambiguous

acceptance_scenarios.given: Required facts, population or inputs are ambiguous
acceptance_scenarios.then: Validate matching state/interaction and resume once.

acceptance_scenarios.given: Required source kinds, fields or mappings are absent or unknown
acceptance_scenarios.then: Keep the requested fact unresolved and name only the absence that the evidence actually establishes. Do not equate an unavailable source with an empty result, and do not treat missing data as permission to build a query.

acceptance_scenarios.given: Data is supported, but no offered query meets the need

acceptance_scenarios.given: Data is supported, but no offered query meets the need
acceptance_scenarios.then: Independently compile/verify, enforce catalog-write permission and resume only a verified version.

acceptance_scenarios.given: The source is stale, unavailable, denied or the budget is exhausted
acceptance_scenarios.when: Stop honestly, without fabricating zero results
acceptance_scenarios.then: Return the actual execution condition and source/budget limitation. A query that ran and found no matching evidence is different from a query that could not be served. A read-only failure does not authorize indexing, publication or catalog mutation.

acceptance_scenarios.given: Evidence or required fields remain incomplete
acceptance_scenarios.when: Partial is an answer condition, not a success badge
acceptance_scenarios.then: Retain the known subset, missing facts and unknown total. Continue only through the existing bounded research/continuation rules when useful work and budget remain; otherwise return partial or unresolved.

acceptance_scenarios.given: Tracing is disabled, fails or is not remotely verified
acceptance_scenarios.then: Keep disabled, unavailable, unverified and verified observation states distinct. Withhold an accessible trace claim until matching remote evidence is independently verified. Preserve one retrieval attempt and a sanitized warning when observation fails.

provenance.note:
Current implementation reference
Committed retrieval and kernel-v01 baseline: e056ccd2996293d0b63f4ae081cc3368f244e11c. The working checkout also contains the tested decision-store integration candidate from a28b1c247ff01fa80adc7464cad93619ff386edb; its merge commit is pending the ADR collision-guard repair approval. The numbered retrieval journey describes the committed baseline and retained tested behavior; the separate decision-memory panel is explicitly candidate-only. This document does not claim the candidate is committed or live-verified. Flow readiness remains draft; AC statuses are derived bookkeeping, not proof labels.

Local-tested mechanisms
Prior saved tests cover answer contracts, source-fit refusal, actual research handoff, fresh-process resumption, budget limits and observation failure boundaries. Tests using controlled storage or scripted Jev prove those boundaries, not live provider quality. [Acceptance matrix](reports/knowledge-answer-acceptance-matrix.json) · [Research tests](reports/knowledge-answer-research-tests.xml). Post-merge verification remains separate.

The v01 merge replay passed 101 tests plus 42 subtests, followed by five focused mixed-source, real chunking and resumed-budget controls. These are local controlled-provider tests. [Merge replay](reports/knowledge-answer-kernel-v01-merge-replay.xml) · [Focused controls](reports/knowledge-answer-reserve-final-controls.xml).

The reviewed decision-store integration candidate passed 293 tests plus 42 subtests, including actual local file publication/reuse and retained retrieval contracts. Jev and host behavior were scripted; no live provider proof is implied. [Decision-store merge tests](reports/knowledge-answer-decision-store-merge-tests.xml).

Live-verified subset
Prior Aura verification at 59269e024e4d0290b68b03d0d382745966e67e29 exercised six direct retrieval canaries. That source revision is historical once the kernel merge changes HEAD; it does not prove the merged whole research/Jev path. The older query-growth Aura receipt also used scripted actors. [Saved growth receipt](reports/knowledge-query-growth-aura.json). [Six direct Aura canaries](reports/knowledge-answer-aura-verification.json).

Not enabled / unknown
Configured real Jev quality and matching remote Langfuse verification were not live-tested in these integration checks. Controlled Jev responses establish routing and boundary behavior only. Production semantic/vector readiness remains a source/model/generation condition, not a catalog capability flag. The decision-store merge is pending; its candidate behavior is described separately below.

How source changes reach retrieval
Index publication is an explicit immutable sync, or the configured main-branch CI trigger when enabled. Editing a working file or environment setting is not a publication event. Existing runs retain their source/generation pins. [Run and publication guide](docs/how-to/run-knowledge-retrieval.md).

Decision memory — tested candidate, merge pending
The reviewed integration candidate adds a file/null ColonyMemory port. The decision LangGraph looks up published human-approved records; Jev judges applicability; a human can confirm reuse. Confirmed reuse may finish without research or retrieval. New human-approved decisions are staged in run artifacts; an explicit decisions publish command makes them available for later runs. Missing or stale indexes yield no precedent with a warning.

This is not Neo4j query-outcome learning: direct knowledge retrieval and the graph-query flow do not consult this memory port or automatically retune ranking. [Decision graph](kernel/capabilities/decision/executor.py) · [Memory and publication](docs/how-to/file-and-reuse-decisions-with-the-kernel.md).

Requested target design — not built
The linked target now includes optional caller keywords, conditional interchangeable-LLM generation of five terms, Jev method/component choice, separate retrieval attempts, original-question comparison, advisory strategy recording and later applicability checking, then combination/deduplication and relevance ranking.

Native term extraction, candidate merging and Jev reranking already exist; semantic mechanisms remain behind readiness gates. The new generative composition and advisory strategy read/write loop are not implemented or evaluated. Current human-approved decision publication is a different contract. No automatic model training or source authority is implied.

Separate host-needs experiment
The [isolated interpreter](docs/product-truth/flows/leafcutter/retrieval-needs-interpretation.flow.json) uses real KernelService/LangGraph host waits and typed resume, exposed only by the experiment registry. It is not part of this baseline's runtime order. The [accepted trial](reports/retrieval-needs-llm-2026-10-03-accepted/README.md) records 12 accepted/completed interpretations, 8/12 frozen semantic passes and a separate 7/7 overlay. Those are dated evidence, not per-call runtime grading or production admission. Existing baseline proof and AC mappings remain unchanged.

Added source-bound field/type/requiredness/default metadata and explicitly illustrative JSON projections. Preserved topology, actor ownership, realization and AC status. Non-JSON artifacts and genuinely undefined proposed interfaces remain explicit.

Document the KM-500e-1-i public needs-to-selection integration against the current contracts. Keep broader target method strategies proposed and Oct3 experimental receipts unchanged. Controlled integration tests and live model quality remain separate evidence.

New blind interpretation evidence is reports/retrieval-public-2026-10-09/needs-evaluation/controller-envelope-repair/summary.json: 16 accepted completed interpretations, 12/12 unchanged baseline checks and 4/4 frozen independent holdouts. An invalid controller actor encoding was repaired by submitting identical response bytes to the same waits; no new model generation. These are interpretation results, not public retrieval, Aura or live Jev proof. Historical Oct3 8/12 is unchanged.

Documented optional field_contents and separate public /test_spec evidence under the existing source and caller budgets. The original reports/retrieval-public-2026-10-09/baseline.html records 0/5 complete positives and a passing stale-source control; baseline-source-comparison.json proves test_spec existed in the pinned source but was lost in disclosure. Final guarded-code evidence at reports/retrieval-public-2026-10-09/final-verification/verified-summary.json completes 2/2 exact-AC cases with/without catalog, matching actual criteria and test_spec, unchanged original blind interpretation responses, and four fresh TypeSafe Jev calls. It uses bounded local actual-source storage, not live Neo4j. Count selection, count budgets, topic-wide discovery and publication remain open; no broad AC completion follows.
